38	- **Update `HANDOFF.md` at the end of EVERY session** — refresh "Current status," git/PR state, and
39	  "What's next" so the next agent (or the owner) is never confused. This is mandatory, not optional.
40	
41	**Git / PR discipline (learned the hard way — do NOT repeat)**
42	- **Branch per change → PR → the _owner_ merges → delete the branch.** Never push straight to `main`.
43	- **Before telling the owner a PR is "ready to merge," push ALL commits and confirm the branch is fully
44	  up to date** — run `git status` (clean) and `git log origin/<branch>..HEAD` (empty). *Why:* a PR was
45	  once merged while later commits were still unpushed, silently dropping a whole work section from
46	  `main`. Verify the remote branch HEAD is what you think it is *before* you say "ready."
47	- **Delete every branch as soon as its PR is merged** — local *and* remote (`git branch -d <b>` +
48	  `git push origin --delete <b>`) — then fast-forward `main`. No merged branch lingers.
49	- If you add commits to a branch *after* its PR was already merged, those commits are NOT in `main`:
50	  open a **new** PR for them (you can't reopen a merged PR).
51	
52	**Build cadence (per component) — explain → align → build → observe → prune**
53	1. **Explain first.** Before writing non-trivial code, describe *what* we're about to build, *why*, a
54	   short **concept primer** for any new tech (Sparkplug B, hypertables, CDC/Debezium, Cypher, ISO
55	   15926, …), and the **alternatives + trade-offs**. Situate it in its charter plane.
56	2. **Align.** Discuss at a high level and confirm the owner understands the concept before coding.
57	3. **Build piece by piece.** Small, reviewable increments. Narrate each block (what it does + why).
58	   Favor explicit, readable code over clever code — this is a teaching codebase.
59	4. **Run & observe.** Actually run it and look at the output together (e.g. `mosquitto_sub` to see
60	   Sparkplug messages, SQL against TimescaleDB, Cypher against Neo4j). Seeing it work cements the why.
61	5. **Prune.** Once aligned and the component is done, remove the teaching scaffolding, keeping only
62	   useful **code documentation** (docstrings + a short component note). Durable concepts/gotchas go to
63	   a **learning log** (`design/LEARNING_LOG.md`) so pruning code never loses the learning.
64	
65	**Medium**
66	- **Marimo notebooks** (via the `marimo-pair` skill) are the interactive surface for learning and
67	  prototyping Python logic — explain/experiment cell by cell.
68	- Infrastructure (brokers, TimescaleDB, OpenPLC, Neo4j, ERPNext) runs as **services** (Docker); the
69	  notebook/package code talks to them as clients.
70	- **Notebook → package (DECIDED):** `notebooks/` holds one Marimo notebook **per component** (rich
71	  explanations, committed, clearly the "learning surface"); `src/scada_harmonizer/` is the **package =
72	  source of truth** where finalized, documented code graduates. When a component is done: prune the
73	  notebook's teaching scaffolding (keep a slim demo or retire it), migrate clean code to `src/`,
74	  durable concepts to `design/LEARNING_LOG.md`.
75	
76	**Diagrams (DECIDED) — use Eraser, save to the `scada_harmonization` workspace**
77	- **All project diagrams are created with the Eraser MCP** — architecture, data-flow, sequence, ER,
78	  ISA-95 topology, knowledge-graph schema, etc. Do **not** produce deliverable diagrams with other
79	  tools or as committed ASCII art. Eraser is the single source of truth for visual artifacts.
80	- **Every diagram is saved to the Eraser workspace/folder named `scada_harmonization`** so all diagrams
81	  live in one place. Always target that folder when calling Eraser.
82	- **One diagram per architecture view.** Each implementation type (hand-built / Python-centric,
83	  UMH-anchored, cloud-native) gets its own full architecture diagram in that workspace (charter §5).
84	- Quick inline **ASCII sketches are fine for discussion**, but the canonical artifact is the Eraser
85	  diagram — embed/link its URL in the relevant `design/*.md` doc so it's discoverable.
86	- The Eraser MCP is registered for all local agents (Claude, Codex, Gemini, Cursor, OpenCode, Kimi,
87	  Hermes); each authenticates via its own OAuth login on first use.
88	
89	**Pace is owner-set.** Pause at natural boundaries; ask "go deeper or move on?" Don't race ahead.
90	
91	**Learning practices**
92	1. **Raw mechanism before convenience wrapper.** Show the actual thing first — a raw `paho-mqtt`
93	   publish + real Sparkplug payload bytes before a helper; raw SQL/Cypher before an ORM. Justify every
94	   dependency ("why this library, what it hides"). Biggest guard against black boxes.
95	2. **Docker Compose is a learning artifact.** Add services one at a time, each explained; the owner
96	   brings them up/down (`! docker compose up …`). The wiring is half the lesson.
97	3. **Running glossary.** Maintain a GLOSSARY in `design/LEARNING_LOG.md`; add plain-language defs as
98	   each term appears (ISA-95, UNS, NBIRTH/DBIRTH, RBE, OLTP/OLAP, WAL, CDC, FLOC, DEXPI, hypertable, …).
99	4. **Tests as executable understanding.** Small targeted tests (e.g. cross-source equivalence) encode
100	   what was learned and can't go stale; borrow the ISHE test strategy.
101	5. **YAGNI / one slice at a time.** Build only what the current phase needs, fully understood. Don't
102	   scaffold later planes early. Depth over breadth.
103	6. **Determinism for re-runs.** Seed randomness; make replays deterministic so re-running a block
104	   while studying it gives the same result.
105	7. **Owner runs things, not just watches.** Where practical the owner executes commands/queries
106	   (`! …`), predicts outputs, and compares. Active recall beats passive narration.
107	8. **Commit history as a learning trail.** Small commits + explanatory messages + the learning log let
108	   the owner later ask "why is this here?" (the `explain` / `what-happened` skills read provenance).
109	
110	**Explicit learn-by-building milestones (do NOT shortcut):** **Debezium** (log-based CDC, Phase 5a),
111	**Redis** (online feature store, Phase 6), **OPC-UA** (real protocol at Geismar, Phase 4), **Spark**

1	# Industrial Data Harmonization & Contextualization Home Lab
2	
3	A home lab that **simulates a multi-site process / specialty-chemicals manufacturer** in which
4	similar operational realities are represented differently across sites — then **harmonizes** those
5	disparate OT representations into a common enterprise language through a Sparkplug B / MQTT
6	**Unified Namespace (UNS)**, and **contextualizes** the result into a knowledge graph meaningful to
7	OT, IT, analytics, ML, ERP, and graph-based reasoning systems.
8	
9	This is a **learning environment and architecture prototype** — built to understand every layer of
10	a modern industrial data stack at the bare-metal level *before* adopting enterprise software that
11	abstracts those layers away.
12	
13	> **Authoritative project definition:** [`design/PROJECT_CHARTER.md`](design/PROJECT_CHARTER.md).
14	> This README is a summary; the charter governs.
15	> **Continuing the work / new agent?** Start with [`HANDOFF.md`](HANDOFF.md) for current status and next steps.
16	
17	## The problem being simulated
18	
19	Different sites, lines, and machines represent the *same underlying reality* differently — local
20	PLC naming, controller memory structures, brownfield integrations, divergent tag taxonomies, and
21	even different integrators per project (so tags diverge *within* a site too). What should be
22	enterprise-comparable data arrives as site-specific, cryptic, inconsistent signals — and the cost is
23	operational: analytics data can take **days to assemble by hand**, real-time data stays **fragmented
24	and "owned" by sites**, and ML can't scale across the enterprise. The lab deliberately manufactures
25	this mess (same reality, different names per site), then proves it can be conformed to one namespace,
26	**governed as a reusable data product**, and enriched into connected context. The problem mirrors
27	real process/CPG transformation discovery (anonymized industry pains); see charter §2.
28	
29	## The three planes
30	
31	Sources span the classic **IT / OT / ET** divide: OT (SCADA/PLC tags), IT (on-prem
32	business-transactional data in PostgreSQL — MES/LIMS/CMMS/quality), and ET (engineering topology).
33	
34	| Plane | What it does | Key tech |
35	|-------|--------------|----------|
36	| **1 — Harmonize** (OT) | synthetic Level 0 → PLC-world disguise → Sparkplug B → UNS; unit/status/timestamp normalization + per-field lineage | OpenPLC + **OPC-UA**, two-tier MQTT (**Mosquitto** edge + **EMQX** central, Python forwarder w/ store-and-forward), Sparkplug B, Ignition, **TimescaleDB**, Grafana |
37	| **2 — Record** (Enterprise) | curated operational events → SAP-like business records | ERPNext |
38	| **3 — Contextualize** (Knowledge) | UNS + IT transactional + ERP + asset topology → **identity reconciliation** → knowledge graph → reasoning | Neo4j (ISO 15926 / DEXPI-aligned ontology), GraphRAG |
39	| **4 — Apply** (Intelligence) | consumes Planes 1–3 — **Track A** traditional ML (predictive maintenance, anomaly, forecasting; **flagship: yield improvement / production-leakage, human-in-the-loop & edge-executed**; scored back to UNS) · **Track B** LLM/GenAI (retrieval, copilot via GraphRAG) | ML stack + LLM/GraphRAG *(tooling deferred to Phases 6–7)* |
40	
41	**Storage by concern (no overlap):** time-series → **TimescaleDB** historian;
42	relational/transactional (OLTP) → **PostgreSQL** (transactional source-of-record + derived ODS, the
43	ODS in its own IT-side Postgres — zone split, charter §14 N16); analytical (OLAP) → **medallion lakehouse** (Bronze/Silver/
44	Gold via **Spark ETL**) + **DuckDB** over Parquet; relationships → Neo4j; enterprise records → ERPNext.
45	Pipeline/infra observability via **Prometheus + Grafana**.
46	
47	## Guiding principle
48	
49	> Only **Level 0 (the physical world)** is synthetic. Everything above — PLC-facing structures,
50	> messaging, historian, analytics, ERP, knowledge graph, cloud — behaves like a real OT/IT stack
51	> assembled from open-source or free/community software.
52	
53	## Data strategy
54	
55	The domain is **data-driven, not dictated**, so realistic data is always available:
56	
57	- **Tennessee Eastman Process** — continuous chemical-process units (reactors, columns, loops)
58	- **Industrial IoT Dataset (Synthetic)** — rotating machines (pumps, compressors, motors)
59	
60	The enterprise is **Lagos Specialty Chemicals** (UNS root `lagos-chem`), operating **4 sites** —
61	**Beaumont** (Allen-Bradley, real OpenPLC/Modbus), **Geismar** (Siemens, real OPC-UA via `asyncua`),
62	**Rotterdam** (Ignition-style), **Corpus Christi** (CygNet) — each running the same units/machines but on a different SCADA lineage
63	with deliberately divergent naming. Physical meaning is *assigned* at the mapping stage, anchored by
64	the **three-stage name mapping table** — `friendly variable → site-specific PLC tag → Sparkplug
65	metric` — which is the spine of the lab. The table doubles as a **governed data-product catalog**
66	(each metric has an owner/"gatekeeper", definition, and lineage), so harmonized signals are reusable
67	without re-interpretation.
68	
69	The generator also produces **synthetic relational tables** (MES/LIMS/CMMS/quality) seeded into
70	Postgres, with their own business keys deliberately *not* aligned to OT identities — extending the
71	"same reality, different representation" principle to transactional data and creating the
72	identity-reconciliation problem at the heart of Plane 3.
73	
74	## Implementation approach
75	
76	The three architecture notes are **phases of one architecture**, not competing projects:
77	
78	- **Build & learn → hand-built + Python-centric.** Wire every component explicitly so each boundary
79	  is visible; Python is a first-class UNS participant, not just glue.
80	- **Abstraction (later) → UMH-anchored.** Replace the hand-wired backbone with United Manufacturing
81	  Hub once the internals are understood *(UMH has pivoted to UMH Core — target under re-validation,
82	  charter §12 #16)*.
83	
84	These styles are captured as **three full architecture diagrams** — hand-built/Python-centric ·
85	UMH-anchored · cloud-native (floci→AWS) — in the Eraser `scada_harmonization` workspace. The design
86	was benchmarked layer-by-layer against a real industrial-products target architecture (charter §13).
87	
88	Every component is upgrade-friendly (OSS broker → enterprise; Ignition Maker → licensed; floci →
89	real AWS) without invalidating the design.
90	
91	## Documentation
92	
93	| Document | Role |
94	|----------|------|
95	| [`design/PROJECT_CHARTER.md`](design/PROJECT_CHARTER.md) | **Authoritative project definition** |
96	| [`design/DOMAIN.md`](design/DOMAIN.md) | Domain narrative — Lagos Specialty Chemicals backstory |
97	| [`design/uns_home_lab_notes.md`](design/uns_home_lab_notes.md) | Vision & high-level scope *(archived — superseded on decided items by the charter)* |
98	| [`design/hand_built_sparkplug_uns_notes.md`](design/hand_built_sparkplug_uns_notes.md) | Architecture: hand-built *(archived — superseded on decided items)* |
99	| [`design/umh_anchored_sparkplug_uns_notes.md`](design/umh_anchored_sparkplug_uns_notes.md) | Architecture: UMH-anchored (abstraction phase) *(archived — UMH product state under re-validation, charter §12 #16)* |
100	| [`design/python_centric_uns_notes.md`](design/python_centric_uns_notes.md) | Implementation philosophy: Python-centric *(archived — superseded on decided items)* |
101	| [`design/synthetic_data_generation_notes.md`](design/synthetic_data_generation_notes.md) | Data strategy & the 6-layer pipeline |
102	
103	## Status
104	
105	Pre-implementation — design and charter complete, all infrastructure decisions resolved (broker,
106	historian, PLC realism, sites/enterprise, Postgres deployment, CDC), and a full **reference-architecture
107	review** done (charter §13: OPC-UA, medallion+Spark, observability, MLflow, alerting, the three
108	implementation variants). Build not yet started; next is Phase 0 (repo skeleton + the three-stage
109	mapping table). See the charter's build sequence (Phases 0–7).
110

**CDC learning milestone (within Phase 5a):**

- **5a.1 — Python poll:** watermark-based polling of the role-A schemas, publishing **Debezium-shaped**
  change events to Kafka — envelope `{before, after, op (c/u/d/r), ts_ms, source}`, topic
  `{server}.{schema}.{table}` (e.g. `lagoschem.mes.work_order`).
- **5a.2 — Debezium sandbox (one table):** stand up **Kafka Connect + Debezium Postgres connector**

# Industrial Data Harmonization & Contextualization Home Lab

A home lab that **simulates a multi-site process / specialty-chemicals manufacturer** in which
similar operational realities are represented differently across sites — then **harmonizes** those
disparate OT representations into a common enterprise language through a Sparkplug B / MQTT
**Unified Namespace (UNS)**, and **contextualizes** the result into a knowledge graph meaningful to
OT, IT, analytics, ML, ERP, and graph-based reasoning systems.

This is a **learning environment and architecture prototype** — built to understand every layer of
a modern industrial data stack at the bare-metal level *before* adopting enterprise software that
abstracts those layers away.

> **Authoritative project definition:** [`design/PROJECT_CHARTER.md`](design/PROJECT_CHARTER.md).
> This README is a summary; the charter governs.
> **Continuing the work / new agent?** Start with [`HANDOFF.md`](HANDOFF.md) for current status and next steps.

## The problem being simulated

Different sites, lines, and machines represent the *same underlying reality* differently — local
PLC naming, controller memory structures, brownfield integrations, divergent tag taxonomies, and
even different integrators per project (so tags diverge *within* a site too). What should be
enterprise-comparable data arrives as site-specific, cryptic, inconsistent signals — and the cost is
operational: analytics data can take **days to assemble by hand**, real-time data stays **fragmented
and "owned" by sites**, and ML can't scale across the enterprise. The lab deliberately manufactures
this mess (same reality, different names per site), then proves it can be conformed to one namespace,
**governed as a reusable data product**, and enriched into connected context. The problem mirrors
real process/CPG transformation discovery (anonymized industry pains); see charter §2.

## The three planes

Sources span the classic **IT / OT / ET** divide: OT (SCADA/PLC tags), IT (on-prem
business-transactional data in PostgreSQL — MES/LIMS/CMMS/quality), and ET (engineering topology).

| Plane | What it does | Key tech |
|-------|--------------|----------|
| **1 — Harmonize** (OT) | synthetic Level 0 → PLC-world disguise → Sparkplug B → UNS; unit/status/timestamp normalization + per-field lineage | OpenPLC + **OPC-UA**, two-tier MQTT (**Mosquitto** edge + **EMQX** central, Python forwarder w/ store-and-forward), Sparkplug B, Ignition, **TimescaleDB**, Grafana |
| **2 — Record** (Enterprise) | curated operational events → SAP-like business records | ERPNext |
| **3 — Contextualize** (Knowledge) | UNS + IT transactional + ERP + asset topology → **identity reconciliation** → knowledge graph → reasoning | Neo4j (ISO 15926 / DEXPI-aligned ontology), GraphRAG |
| **4 — Apply** (Intelligence) | consumes Planes 1–3 — **Track A** traditional ML (predictive maintenance, anomaly, forecasting; **flagship: yield improvement / production-leakage, human-in-the-loop & edge-executed**; scored back to UNS) · **Track B** LLM/GenAI (retrieval, copilot via GraphRAG) | ML stack + LLM/GraphRAG *(tooling deferred to Phases 6–7)* |

**Storage by concern (no overlap):** time-series → **TimescaleDB** historian;
relational/transactional (OLTP) → **PostgreSQL** (transactional source-of-record + derived ODS, the
ODS in its own IT-side Postgres — zone split, charter §14 N16); analytical (OLAP) → **medallion lakehouse** (Bronze/Silver/
Gold via **Spark ETL**) + **DuckDB** over Parquet; relationships → Neo4j; enterprise records → ERPNext.
Pipeline/infra observability via **Prometheus + Grafana**.

## Guiding principle

> Only **Level 0 (the physical world)** is synthetic. Everything above — PLC-facing structures,
> messaging, historian, analytics, ERP, knowledge graph, cloud — behaves like a real OT/IT stack
> assembled from open-source or free/community software.

## Data strategy

The domain is **data-driven, not dictated**, so realistic data is always available:

- **Tennessee Eastman Process** — continuous chemical-process units (reactors, columns, loops)
- **Industrial IoT Dataset (Synthetic)** — rotating machines (pumps, compressors, motors)

The enterprise is **Lagos Specialty Chemicals** (UNS root `lagos-chem`), operating **4 sites** —
**Beaumont** (Allen-Bradley, real OpenPLC/Modbus), **Geismar** (Siemens, real OPC-UA via `asyncua`),
**Rotterdam** (Ignition-style), **Corpus Christi** (CygNet) — each running the same units/machines but on a different SCADA lineage
with deliberately divergent naming. Physical meaning is *assigned* at the mapping stage, anchored by
the **three-stage name mapping table** — `friendly variable → site-specific PLC tag → Sparkplug
metric` — which is the spine of the lab. The table doubles as a **governed data-product catalog**
(each metric has an owner/"gatekeeper", definition, and lineage), so harmonized signals are reusable
without re-interpretation.

The generator also produces **synthetic relational tables** (MES/LIMS/CMMS/quality) seeded into
Postgres, with their own business keys deliberately *not* aligned to OT identities — extending the
"same reality, different representation" principle to transactional data and creating the
identity-reconciliation problem at the heart of Plane 3.

## Implementation approach

The three architecture notes are **phases of one architecture**, not competing projects:

- **Build & learn → hand-built + Python-centric.** Wire every component explicitly so each boundary
  is visible; Python is a first-class UNS participant, not just glue.
- **Abstraction (later) → UMH-anchored.** Replace the hand-wired backbone with United Manufacturing
  Hub once the internals are understood *(UMH has pivoted to UMH Core — target under re-validation,
  charter §12 #16)*.

These styles are captured as **three full architecture diagrams** — hand-built/Python-centric ·
UMH-anchored · cloud-native (floci→AWS) — in the Eraser `scada_harmonization` workspace. The design
was benchmarked layer-by-layer against a real industrial-products target architecture (charter §13).

Every component is upgrade-friendly (OSS broker → enterprise; Ignition Maker → licensed; floci →
real AWS) without invalidating the design.

|----------|------|
| [`design/PROJECT_CHARTER.md`](design/PROJECT_CHARTER.md) | **Authoritative project definition** |
| [`design/DOMAIN.md`](design/DOMAIN.md) | Domain narrative — Lagos Specialty Chemicals backstory |

| [`design/python_centric_uns_notes.md`](design/python_centric_uns_notes.md) | Implementation philosophy: Python-centric *(archived — superseded on decided items)* |
| [`design/synthetic_data_generation_notes.md`](design/synthetic_data_generation_notes.md) | Data strategy & the 6-layer pipeline |

### This session (2026-07-06) — IT/OT best-practice review adopted (charter §14 + §4.1)

Ran a deep multi-lens best-practice review (UNS/Sparkplug · IEC 62443/Purdue zoning · ISA-95/-88
modeling · streaming/lakehouse · historian ops · industrial-ML safety · tool fact-check · plan
integrity; all web-verified) of every design doc. **The architecture was validated** (forwarder-not-
bridge, EMQX-in-iDMZ, Z3/Z4 zoning, P8, graded HITL all match or exceed published practice); the
genuine gaps were adopted as **charter §14 (ledger N1–N35)**. Highlights:

- **N1/N2 — Sparkplug↔ISA-95 namespace encoding decided** (the §6 `lagos-chem/...` root vs Sparkplug's
  fixed `spBv1.0/...` topics were incompatible as written): site tier = pure Sparkplug
  (`group_id=lagos-chem:<site>`); enterprise tier = retained plain-MQTT ISA-95 republish on EMQX.
- **N3–N5** — forwarder = compliant Edge Node per site (bdSeq/seq/alias remap/NCMD Rebirth/
  `is_historical` flush); Primary Host named per tier; closed-loop commands are **NCMD/DCMD**, not
  "setpoint topics" (L6.5 amended).
- **N8–N12** — replay clock decided (TEP is 3-minute data → re-classed; simulated clock w/ rebasing);
  at-least-once + idempotent sinks; **quality model** (Good/Uncertain/Bad/Stale = 5th divergence
  dimension); historian lifecycle; store-and-forward semantics.
- **N13–N20** — **lot-based MES** (continuous process; ISA-88 out, ISA-106 in; `mes.production_lot` +
  material model); identity_map survivorship; **`ods_core` split to an IT-side Postgres** (zone fix,
  amends #7); Beaumont raw-counts scaling; UNECE units; ISA-18.2 alarm model.
- **N21–N25** — conduit inventory + "no IT-initiated connections into OT" rule; broker authn +
  per-branch ACLs; TLS on forwarder→EMQX; `command_audit`; **SIS/GuardLogix conflation corrected**
  (BPCS-level guard; IEC 61511 note).
- **N26–N35** — Apicurio schema registry (5a.2); Bronze immutable-raw; dead-letter redrive; CDC ops
  specifics; **L0 Shadow HITL rung**; ML drift monitoring + delayed-label eval; recommendation TTL;
  **multivariate SPC (PCA T²/SPE)**; dataset versioning + model cards; feature single-sourcing.
- **Tool/version reality (charter §4.1 pinned stack):** EMQX ≥5.9 **BSL 1.1 single-node** (the old
  "EMQX OSS bridges+clustering" justification was factually wrong); PySparkplug 0.6.x downgraded to
  *candidate* (Pre-Alpha); TimescaleDB Community ≥2.26 / TigerData; **UMH pivoted to UMH Core** (new
  open decision §12 #16 — re-validate before Diagram 2); Redis 8 AGPLv3; ERPNext v15/16; Ignition
  Maker 8.3 gotchas; floci fallback.
- **Plan:** Phase 4 split into **4a/4b/4c**; per-phase **exit criteria** (§8.1); **risk register**
  (§8.2 — incl. the 16–24 GB RAM reality → compose profiles per phase); staleness sweep (Geismar
  OPC-UA drift, archived-note banners, stray `</content>`/`DOCEOF` artifacts); `LEARNING_LOG.md`
  seeded.

## What this is

Adoption of the 2026-07-06 multi-lens IT/OT best-practice review (UNS/Sparkplug · IEC 62443/Purdue · ISA-95/-88 · streaming/lakehouse · historian ops · industrial-ML safety · tool fact-check · plan integrity — all web-verified against standards and vendor sources). The review **validated the architecture**; this PR closes the genuine gaps and fixes everything stale. Four themed commits:

### 1 — Staleness & integrity sweep
- Geismar drift fixed everywhere (real OPC-UA per §13 L1.1 — charter §6/§12, AGENTS, DOMAIN, README, HANDOFF)
- Charter §12 reordered numerically; archived banners on the four vision notes; stray `</content>`/`DOCEOF` artifacts removed; wrong §13.7 cross-ref fixed; `design/LEARNING_LOG.md` seeded

### 2 — Tool & version reality (names + versions everywhere)
- **New charter §4.1 pinned stack** — 23 tools with version floors, editions, licenses, phases
- **EMQX**: factually wrong justification corrected → pinned **≥5.9, BSL 1.1, single node** (pre-5.9 OSS had no Kafka/Postgres bridges; clustering is paid)
- **PySparkplug 0.6.x** downgraded to *candidate* (PyPI Pre-Alpha) with a Phase-2 spec-conformance test + fallbacks
- **TimescaleDB Community ≥2.26** (TSL; TigerData rename) on PostgreSQL ≥17.2 · **UMH Core pivot** recorded (new open decision §12 #16 — re-validate before Diagram 2) · Redis 8 AGPLv3 · ERPNext v15/16 · Ignition Maker 8.3 gotchas · floci fallback

### 3 — Charter §14: 35 new decisions (N1–N35)
- **UNS/Sparkplug (N1–N7):** ISA-95↔Sparkplug namespace encoding (site tier = pure Sparkplug, enterprise tier = retained ISA-95 republish — resolves the `lagos-chem/...` vs `spBv1.0/...` contradiction); retained-state semantics corrected; forwarder = compliant Edge Node (bdSeq/seq/alias/NCMD-Rebirth/`is_historical`); Primary Hosts; **commands are NCMD/DCMD**; Python UNS→Kafka decode bridge + topic/key design; Sparkplug Templates
- **Time/quality/historian (N8–N12):** replay clock (TEP = 3-min data, re-classed); idempotent sinks; quality model (5th divergence dimension); historian lifecycle; store-and-forward semantics
- **Data modeling (N13–N20):** **lot-based MES** (continuous process — ISA-106), material model, MDM survivorship, **ods_core → IT-side Postgres** (zone fix, amends #7), Beaumont raw-counts scaling, UNECE units, ISA-18.2 alarms
- **Security (N21–N25):** conduit inventory + no-IT-into-OT rule; broker auth + per-branch ACLs; TLS on the WAN conduit; `command_audit`; **SIS/GuardLogix conflation corrected** (IEC 61511)
- **Streaming/ML (N26–N35):** Apicurio registry; Bronze immutable-raw; dead-letter redrive; CDC ops; **L0 Shadow HITL rung**; drift monitoring; recommendation TTL; **multivariate SPC (T²/SPE)**; dataset versioning + model cards; feature single-sourcing

### 4 — Plan restructure
- Phase 4 → **4a/4b/4c** (thesis proof first, real protocols second, resilience third)
- **§8.1 exit criteria** per phase · **§8.2 risk register** (incl. the 16–24 GB RAM reality → compose profiles)
- **Resequenced:** Phase 0 starts when Diagram 1 locks; Diagrams 2–3 just-in-time
- HANDOFF: session entry + §14 gap-checklist mapped onto the Diagram-1 walkthrough blocks

## Review guide
The charter diff is large but ledger-shaped: start with §14, then §4.1, then the §8 changes; everything else is mirrors/amendments pointing back at N-items.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -2

Benthos-UMH can be configured and deployed via the Management Console, allowing any number of protocol converters to be configured directly from the Management Console. Benthos-UMH can be deployed as a standalone Docker container or directly from the Management Console.

18

20	PLC naming, controller memory structures, brownfield integrations, divergent tag taxonomies, and
21	even different integrators per project (so tags diverge *within* a site too). What should be
22	enterprise-comparable data arrives as site-specific, cryptic, inconsistent signals — and the cost is
23	operational: analytics data can take **days to assemble by hand**, real-time data stays **fragmented
24	and "owned" by sites**, and ML can't scale across the enterprise. The lab deliberately manufactures
25	this mess (same reality, different names per site), then proves it can be conformed to one namespace,
26	**governed as a reusable data product**, and enriched into connected context. The problem mirrors
27	real process/CPG transformation discovery (anonymized industry pains); see charter §2.
28	
29	## The three planes
30	
31	Sources span the classic **IT / OT / ET** divide: OT (SCADA/PLC tags), IT (on-prem
32	business-transactional data in PostgreSQL — MES/LIMS/CMMS/quality), and ET (engineering topology).

37	| **2 — Record** (Enterprise) | curated operational events → SAP-like business records | ERPNext |
38	| **3 — Contextualize** (Knowledge) | UNS + IT transactional + ERP + asset topology → **identity reconciliation** → knowledge graph → reasoning | Neo4j (ISO 15926 / DEXPI-aligned ontology), GraphRAG |
39	| **4 — Apply** (Intelligence) | consumes Planes 1–3 — **Track A** traditional ML (predictive maintenance, anomaly, forecasting; **flagship: yield improvement / production-leakage, human-in-the-loop & edge-executed**; scored back to UNS) · **Track B** LLM/GenAI (retrieval, copilot via GraphRAG) | ML stack + LLM/GraphRAG *(tooling deferred to Phases 6–7)* |
40	
41	**Storage by concern (no overlap):** time-series → **TimescaleDB** historian;
42	relational/transactional (OLTP) → **PostgreSQL** (transactional source-of-record + derived ODS, the
43	ODS in its own IT-side Postgres — zone split, charter §14 N16); analytical (OLAP) → **medallion lakehouse** (Bronze/Silver/
44	Gold via **Spark ETL**) + **DuckDB** over Parquet; relationships → Neo4j; enterprise records → ERPNext.
45	Pipeline/infra observability via **Prometheus + Grafana**.
46	
47	## Guiding principle
48	
49	> Only **Level 0 (the physical world)** is synthetic. Everything above — PLC-facing structures,
50	> messaging, historian, analytics, ERP, knowledge graph, cloud — behaves like a real OT/IT stack
51	> assembled from open-source or free/community software.
52	
53	## Data strategy
54	
55	The domain is **data-driven, not dictated**, so realistic data is always available:
56	
57	- **Tennessee Eastman Process** — continuous chemical-process units (reactors, columns, loops)
58	- **Industrial IoT Dataset (Synthetic)** — rotating machines (pumps, compressors, motors)
59	
60	The enterprise is **Lagos Specialty Chemicals** (UNS root `lagos-chem`), operating **4 sites** —
61	**Beaumont** (Allen-Bradley, real OpenPLC/Modbus), **Geismar** (Siemens, real OPC-UA via `asyncua`),
62	**Rotterdam** (Ignition-style), **Corpus Christi** (CygNet) — each running the same units/machines but on a different SCADA lineage
63	with deliberately divergent naming. Physical meaning is *assigned* at the mapping stage, anchored by
64	the **three-stage name mapping table** — `friendly variable → site-specific PLC tag → Sparkplug
65	metric` — which is the spine of the lab. The table doubles as a **governed data-product catalog**
66	(each metric has an owner/"gatekeeper", definition, and lineage), so harmonized signals are reusable
67	without re-interpretation.
68	
69	The generator also produces **synthetic relational tables** (MES/LIMS/CMMS/quality) seeded into
70	Postgres, with their own business keys deliberately *not* aligned to OT identities — extending the
71	"same reality, different representation" principle to transactional data and creating the
72	identity-reconciliation problem at the heart of Plane 3.
73

37	**Session discipline**
38	- **Update `HANDOFF.md` at the end of EVERY session** — refresh "Current status," git/PR state, and
39	  "What's next" so the next agent (or the owner) is never confused. This is mandatory, not optional.
40	
41	**Git / PR discipline (learned the hard way — do NOT repeat)**
42	- **Branch per change → PR → the _owner_ merges → delete the branch.** Never push straight to `main`.
43	- **Before telling the owner a PR is "ready to merge," push ALL commits and confirm the branch is fully
44	  up to date** — run `git status` (clean) and `git log origin/<branch>..HEAD` (empty). *Why:* a PR was
45	  once merged while later commits were still unpushed, silently dropping a whole work section from
46	  `main`. Verify the remote branch HEAD is what you think it is *before* you say "ready."
47	- **Delete every branch as soon as its PR is merged** — local *and* remote (`git branch -d <b>` +
48	  `git push origin --delete <b>`) — then fast-forward `main`. No merged branch lingers.
49	- If you add commits to a branch *after* its PR was already merged, those commits are NOT in `main`:
50	  open a **new** PR for them (you can't reopen a merged PR).
51	
52	**Build cadence (per component) — explain → align → build → observe → prune**
53	1. **Explain first.** Before writing non-trivial code, describe *what* we're about to build, *why*, a
54	   short **concept primer** for any new tech (Sparkplug B, hypertables, CDC/Debezium, Cypher, ISO
55	   15926, …), and the **alternatives + trade-offs**. Situate it in its charter plane.
56	2. **Align.** Discuss at a high level and confirm the owner understands the concept before coding.
57	3. **Build piece by piece.** Small, reviewable increments. Narrate each block (what it does + why).
58	   Favor explicit, readable code over clever code — this is a teaching codebase.
59	4. **Run & observe.** Actually run it and look at the output together (e.g. `mosquitto_sub` to see
60	   Sparkplug messages, SQL against TimescaleDB, Cypher against Neo4j). Seeing it work cements the why.
61	5. **Prune.** Once aligned and the component is done, remove the teaching scaffolding, keeping only
62	   useful **code documentation** (docstrings + a short component note). Durable concepts/gotchas go to
63	   a **learning log** (`design/LEARNING_LOG.md`) so pruning code never loses the learning.

66	- **Marimo notebooks** (via the `marimo-pair` skill) are the interactive surface for learning and
67	  prototyping Python logic — explain/experiment cell by cell.
68	- Infrastructure (brokers, TimescaleDB, OpenPLC, Neo4j, ERPNext) runs as **services** (Docker); the
69	  notebook/package code talks to them as clients.

78	  ISA-95 topology, knowledge-graph schema, etc. Do **not** produce deliverable diagrams with other

Both questions answered, and the second one is now recorded in the PR:

**1. Yes — PR [#17](https://github.com/aadehamid/scada_harmonization/pull/17) is yours to merge.** It's a single PR (per your choice of one-PR-with-themed-commits), now five commits: staleness sweep → tool/version pins → charter §14 decisions → plan restructure → the UMH Core adoption below. The branch is pushed and fully up to date (clean status, zero unpushed commits). Once you merge, I'll delete the branch and fast-forward `main` per your workflow.

**2. Yes, we can adopt UMH Core — and I've recorded that decision (§12 #16 → DECIDED) as commit 5 on the PR.** On the open-source question, verified today:

- **`umh-core` and `benthos-umh` are Apache-2.0** — genuinely open source, per the [UMH GitHub repo](https://github.com/united-manufacturing-hub/united-manufacturing-hub) and [benthos-umh](https://github.com/united-manufacturing-hub/benthos-umh).
- **Two nuances worth knowing:** the **embedded Redpanda** broker inside Core is *source-available* (Redpanda Community License — free to self-host, but not OSI open source), and the cloud **[Management Console](https://mgmt.docs.umh.app/docs/account-and-licensing/) is an optional SaaS** with account-based licensing. Core [runs standalone via YAML config](https://umh.docs.umh.app/docs/features/connectivity/benthos-umh/) without it — that's what the charter now specifies, so the lab stays fully self-hosted.
- **What adopting Core actually means for your abstraction phase** (this changed from the old notes): Core replaces your Python site-forwarders/protocol converters and the UNS→Kafka bridge (benthos-umh Data Flow Components — including a stateful Sparkplug B input that tracks births/aliases/seq, plus Modbus and OPC-UA inputs) and the streaming leg (embedded Redpanda). It does **not** hand you the old Classic TimescaleDB+Grafana bundle — your historian and dashboards stay hand-built. That's arguably a better fit for the lab's thesis anyway: you build the forwarder bare-metal first, then watch a platform abstract exactly that piece.

Sources: [UMH GitHub](https://github.com/united-manufacturing-hub/united-manufacturing-hub) · [benthos-umh](https://github.com/united-manufacturing-hub/benthos-umh) · [benthos-umh docs](https://umh.docs.umh.app/docs/features/connectivity/benthos-umh/) · [Management Console licensing](https://mgmt.docs.umh.app/docs/account-and-licensing/)

Ready for the Diagram 1 walkthrough whenever you are. Suggested flow: merge PR #17 first (so the walkthrough works against the corrected charter), then we go block by block per the HANDOFF §3 agenda — problem tie-in → mechanism → research → gap check → teach-back — with the §14 gap checklist telling us exactly what to fix in Eraser per block (namespace labels, EMQX "cluster"→single node, DCMD command arrows, `ods_core` zone move, and so on).
